links.reason: Both put blame on the withholder: 196 says ஒல்லுவது இல்லென மறுத்தல் brings புரப்போர் புகழ்குறை, and 1051 says கரப்பின் அவர்பழி. But 196 also declares an honest refusal (ஒல்லாது இல்லென மறுத்தல்) a proper part of a giver's friendship, which limits the Kural's rule rather than agreeing with it; the teaches sentence misses this and its claim that the poem used the rule 'before it became a maxim' is not something either text shows.

The image is distinctive and shared in nearly the same words: இடம்பட வீழ்ந்தென அன்று அவண் உண்ணாதாகி (190) and இடம்வீழ்ந்தது உண்ணாது இறக்கும் (N300). The teaches is accurate: the Naladiyar applies it to one's own மானம், while 190 uses the tiger to name the உரனுடையாளர் whose கேண்மை the speaker wants.

The bowed head is genuinely shared (சிறிய இறைஞ்சினள் தலையே; இறைஞ்சினாள்). But 230 gives no sign that the gesture is unreadable: the hero's பெரிய எவ்வம் follows from the parting the thurai names (கண்ணுற்று நீங்கும்), and the checked tears (பனிவரல் ஒடுக்கி) read as feeling, not refusal. The claim that the maxim is 'a reading made after the fact' is the marker's inference, not the poem's.

Thazhumban's ஊணூர் is a real shared name (வாய்மொழித் தழும்பன் ஊணூர் அன்ன in 348; தழும்பன் ... ஊணூர் உம்பர் in 227). But in 227 Unur is not the scale of comparison: it locates Marungur, and the clamour is likened to மருங்கூர்ப் பட்டினத்து எல்லுமிழ் ஆவணத்து அன்ன. The teaches says akam poets reused the town as a scale of plenty, which fits 348 (itself a puram poem) but not what 227 does with it.

Kural 759 says wealth is the sharpest steel for cutting enemies' செருக்கு; it says nothing about leaving home or anyone left behind. 239 is the hero recalling her plea நீட்டுவிர் அல்லிரோ as he goes for பொருள். The only bond is the topic of seeking wealth, and the teaches dresses that shared topic as a condition on the Kural.

186 says மன்னன் உயிர்த்தே மலர்தலை உலகம், 187 that the land is good எவ்வழி நல்லவர் ஆடவர், naming no king; the two adjacent பொருண்மொழிக் காஞ்சி poems do place the land's good in different hands. The pairing teaches something neither shows alone, and the type fits: 187 limits the dependence 186 lays on the king.

Both rank a value above survival: சாதலின் இன்னாதது இல்லை இனிததூஉம் ஈதல் இயையாக்கடை, and ஊன்ஓம்பும் வாழ்க்கை is no மருந்து when பீடு is lost. Giving and honour are both moral domains, so parallel_domain overstates the gap; this is a plain agreement within the Kural. The link also does not start from a Sangam verse.

Kapilar's நள்ளி நளிமுகை உடைந்த நறுங்கார் அடுக்கத்து ... காந்தள் ... நாறும் நறுநுதல் and Paranar's நள்ளி சோலை அடுக்கத்து ... கடவுட் காந்தள் ... ஆய்மலர் நாறி both give a woman's scent (forehead in 238, the hair and shoulders in 152) the kaanthal of Nalli's slopes. The same patron's hill and flower in two poets is a specific, meaningful shared figure.

Both have evening and cold (பனிகடி கொண்ட பண்பில் வாடை மருளின் மாலை; பனிஅரும்பிப் பைதல்கொள் மாலை) worsen the woman's grief, which is the stock situation of separation. The teaches claims the couplet 'presupposes the landscape', which neither verse shows; the pairing only notes the same situation.

Pazhaiyan is named in both (பழையன் பட்டென in 44; மழைத்தோற் பழையன் காவிரி வைப்பின் போஒர் அன்ன in 186), and 44's Chenni avenging him makes it likely the same Chola-side chief. But the teaches asserts that 186 drew on his fame 'before' his fall, a sequence neither poem fixes, and the note does not say what 186 does with Por: the parathai's boast that he cannot break her bangle as none breaks Por.
links.text_issue: Colophon thinai of 44 is flagged (commentary gives பாலை).

links.reason: Both are Kapilar offering Pari's daughters: யானே பரிசிலன் மன்னும் அந்தணன் ... நினக்கியான் கொடுப்பக் கொண்மதி (200) and யானே தந்தை தோழன் இவர் என் மகளிர் அந்தணன் புலவன் கொண்டுவந்தனனே ... யான்தர இவரைக் கொண்மதி (201). 201 adds the claim of the father's friendship and calls the girls his own, a real development of the grounds of the gift. 'Not a kinsman' slightly understates 201's இவர் என் மகளிர், but the teaches holds.

The claim and even its shape match: உண்டால் அம்ம இவ்வுலகம் ... பிறர்க்கென முயலுநர் உண்மையானே and பண்புடையார்ப் பட்டுண்டு உலகம். 182 spells out the conduct (தமியர் உண்டலும் இலரே, புகழ்எனின் உயிருங் கொடுக்குவர், பழியெனின் உலகுடன் பெறினும் கொள்ளலர்), which gives the Kural's abstract பண்பு a concrete content, as the teaches says.

The suppliant-as-bird is shared, but the birds differ (198's துளிநசைப் புள் that lives on raindrops; 199's கலிகொள் புள்ளினம் at a fruiting banyan), so it is a common figure, not one distinctive image. The contrast of postures the teaches draws (மறவாதீமே against நெருநல் உண்டனம் என்னாது) is true, though 'what decides between them is the patron' goes beyond the poems.

The verbal echo is real: வெண்குடைச் செல்வம் வியத்தலோ இலமே (197) and பெரியோரை வியத்தலும் இலமே (192). But 197 then does marvel (எம்மால் வியக்கப் படூஉமோரே) at small chiefs who know பாடு, which departs from 192's refusal to admire or despise anyone; and nothing shows Kumaranar turning Kaniyan's stance into practice, so the direction the teaches asserts is unsupported.

The two couplets share the complaint that one's own நெஞ்சு is not one's own (நீ எமக்கு ஆகாதது; நெஞ்சம் தமரல் வழி). The teaches rests wholly on Parimelazhagar's assignment of speakers, which is commentary, not the verse; 1300 as written is a general maxim. The link does not start from a Sangam verse.

The child's small hand in the food is the same distinctive image: சிறுகை நீட்டி இட்டும் தொட்டும் கவ்வியும் துழந்தும் (188) and மக்கள் சிறுகை அளாவிய கூழ் (64). The teaches is accurate: the Kural makes it a measure of sweetness (அமிழ்தினும் இனிது), 188 makes its absence a verdict (பயக்குறை இல்லை தாம் வாழும் நாளே).

Both are the friend's assurance that he will come back, which is the thurai's stock situation. 237's point is that even rich உறந்தை (as wealth, the object of his வினை) will not keep him from her mouth, not a fear of 'pleasure'; neither poem extends the other, so 'develops' and the 'two fears' teaches overstate a shared situation.

Water and hill appear in both lists (மணிநீரும் ... மலையும்; இருபுனலும் வாய்ந்த மலையும்), but a list of terrain features is not a distinctive image. The teaches is true and modest: 737 names the fort among the land's limbs and 742 makes the terrain the fort's. Kural to Kural, not from a Sangam verse.

The two poems share near-identical lines: அன்னி குறுக்கைப் பறந்தலைத் திதியன் தொல்நிலை முழுமுதல் துமியப் பண்ணி ... புன்னை. 45 makes the gossip louder than the வயிரியர் clamour of that day; 145 has the foster mother wish on the hand that beat her girl the fate of that felled tree (கடுநவைப் படீஇயர்). Two opposite uses of one puram event is exactly what the pair shows.

யாதும் ஊரே (192) and யாதானும் நாடாமால் ஊராமால் (397) make the same claim of belonging everywhere. The Kural ties it to learning (கல்லாதவாறு), 192 to seeing that தீதும் நன்றும் பிறர்தர வாரா. The note's 'no condition of learning' is a little loose, since 192 credits திறவோர் காட்சி, but the teaches already frames it as insight and holds.

The ranking is the same: உணர்ச்சியில்லோர் உடைமை உள்ளேம்; நல்லறிவுடையோர் நல்குரவு உள்ளுதும் உவந்து (197) and நல்லார்கண் பட்ட வறுமையின் இன்னாதே கல்லார்கண் பட்ட திரு (408). Seeing it spoken to a king's face (பெரும!) shows the maxim as a bard's stance, though the word 'first' in the teaches is a chronological claim neither text fixes.

Both use the fruiting tree for the giver's wealth: பயன்மரம் உள்ளூர்ப் பழுத்தற்றால் (216) and the கடவுள் ஆலத்துத் தடவுச்சினைப் பல்பழம் that birds return to (199). The teaches is accurate that one looks from the tree's side and one from the birds', and 199's உடைமை ஆகும் அவர் உடைமை completes the gift relation the Kural states.

Both name Karikal's battle at வெண்ணி: 246 makes the gossip louder than the clamour of Azhundur when Karikal broke the kings there, 55 recalls the சான்றோர் who died with Cheralathan as he sat வடக்கிருந்து, the death her own life refuses to follow. Victor's noise and loser's companions are indeed taken from the two sides; the note's 'the Chera's death measures grief' is slightly loose since it is the followers' death.

542 sets வானோக்கி வாழும் உலகு beside கோல்நோக்கி வாழுங் குடி as parallels; 186 denies நெல் and நீர் the name of life and gives it to the மன்னன், then makes it the king's கடன் to know it. The ranking over food and water and the turn to duty are a real difference the pair shows; it limits the parallel more than it develops it.

The situation is the same (the king's war, then home): வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் மனைகலந்து மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து and வந்துவினை முடித்தனன் வேந்தனும் ... இன்துயில் பெறவே. But the Kural is a wish during unfinished war (வென்றீக), 44 a return after it is won; the teaches calls the couplet the formula 'reduced', which neither text shows, and misses that difference.
links.text_issue: Colophon thinai of 44 is flagged (commentary gives பாலை).

links.reason: Both condemn the king's excess take: 552 likens it to a robber's இடு at spear-point; 184 likens it to யானை புக்க புலம், where தானும் உண்ணான் உலகமும் கெடுமே. The teaches is accurate and specific: the Kural's ground is moral (from the subject), 184's is prudential (from the king's own interest).

Both name செழியன் and முசிறி: 57's செழியன் முதுநீர் முன்றுறை முசிறி முற்றி ... அரும்புண் உறுநரின் வருந்தினள், and 149's முசிறி ஆர்ப்பெழ வளைஇ ... படிமம் வவ்விய ... செழியன். This is a real historical witness, but in 149 the siege is an epithet in a chain locating Koodal and the hill, not an image of suffering; the note does not say what 149 does with it and the teaches overstates it.

The phrasing matches closely: 'இல்லோர்க்கு இல்' என்று இயைவது கரத்தல் வல்லா நெஞ்சம் (53) and இலனென்னும் எவ்வம் உரையாமை ஈதல் (223). In 53 that very virtue sends him across the waste for wealth (நம்மினும் பொருளே காதலர் காதல்), a cost the Kural's praise does not count, so the teaches is true and specific.

The reason for parting is the same heroic aim: நல்லிசை வலித்த நாணுடை மனத்தர் with இல்லிருந்து அமைவோர்க்கு இல் (231) and உரன்நசைஇ உள்ளம் துணையாகச் சென்றார் (1263). The friend uses it to promise return; the Kural's woman merely survives on longing (வரல்நசைஇ இன்னும் உளேன்). That contrast is real, so the pairing teaches something, though it is not plain agreement.

Both refuse the straying husband (நண்ணேன் பரத்தநின் மார்பு; சென்றீ பெரும நிற் றகைக்குநர் யாரோ), the stock marutham situation. The grounds differ (women's eyes feeding on him; a reported வதுவை) and the teaches only says the couplet 'compresses' the scene, which is the shared situation restated, not something the pair shows.

1138 says காமம் மறையிறந்து மன்று படும் whatever one's restraint; in 52 the pallor is already visible (உண்கண் பசலை) yet the heroine forbids the friend to name it காம நோய் even at the cost of இன்உயிர். The two treat the situation differently and the teaches is a real sharpening. Per the colophon she speaks knowing the friend will disclose, which the teaches does not contradict.

poems.note: The cow with its tethered calf is joined to the mother by the comparison -இன்; the thirsty deer only colour the road.
The girl's cry for vengai flowers taken for a tiger's threat maps to the heroine's pallor that may be misread and the household roused; reading it as ullurai needs the thurai's disclosure situation.
The rain on parched land is joined to her joy by -அற்று, an open comparison.
The Katti episode is an open comparison of the gossip (ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே).

ullurai.anchor: ஒருத்தியை நம்மனைத் தந்து வதுவை அயர்ந்தனை என்ப

iraicchi.act: At lamp-lighting the red-legged dove cock calls its beloved mate in the tall house.
iraicchi.sense: While the dove is with its mate at dusk, she weeps alone asking where he is, so he must hurry home to her.

poems.note: The koel only sings; its call marks the spring he promised, mood rather than an act.

iraicchi.act: The tusker bends the tall yaa so his young she-elephant can eat its leaves, and fans the bees off her.
iraicchi.sense: The man on that road will see a beast tending its mate and so cannot forget her; the friend points to it to comfort her.

poems.note: The Mal likeness (மாஅல் போல) is an open simile inside the iraicchi.

iraicchi.act: The doe, glad of union with the buck, leaps without fear at dusk.
iraicchi.sense: The creatures are together at evening while his wife waits pale, so the chariot must hasten to her.

iraicchi.act: The male vulture, wings scorched, sits looking at the face of its mate in the burning desert.
iraicchi.sense: Even the vulture keeps by its mate in hardship, so the heart should not leave her for wealth.

iraicchi.act: The she-elephant worn by summer bathes in the flood with her tusker.
iraicchi.sense: In the rains mates are together, and the hero, at home with her, pities those who leave their partner for wealth.

poems.note: The pair is the cloud's purpose (படீஇய) rather than a seen act, which makes the tag less firm.
The forge bellows and the Venni likeness are open comparisons.
The likeness is to a remembered woman, joined by அன்ன, not a native thing.

iraicchi.act: At dusk the milch herd hurries home, udders swelling, lowing for the tethered calves.
iraicchi.sense: As the cows hasten to their calves, he must hasten home to the wife who coaxes their son with the moon.

poems.note: A herd moving as one is taken as a single carrier.
